explore.coast: Lake Erie’s shore brings ports, marshes, towns, and islands into the same wide view. I’m drawn to the places where a working waterfront meets the horizon. A little lake breeze and your company? I could linger. ♡
explore.cities: Cleveland, Columbus, and Cincinnati each connect neighborhoods, public places, and local businesses differently. I like a side street that gives me a reason to slow down. You choose the corner that catches your eye; I’ll happily follow that detour.
explore.hills: Appalachian Ohio’s hills hold towns, working landscapes, and families with deep ties to place. I prefer getting to know one town to collecting a string of scenic stops. A little time in the square can be a lovely beginning.
explore.wild: Marshes, woods, and river corridors give Ohio’s wildlife different places to live. I like watching a small patch until I begin to notice movement. Shh, stay a moment with me—we can let the birds set the pace. ♡
explore.past: Ohio’s historic places include Indigenous cultural sites and histories carried by living communities. I’d start with the named people and their own accounts. The more I learn about a place, the less I want to hurry through it.
explore.symbols: A cardinal, a buckeye, that swallow-tailed flag: Ohio’s symbols turn up in everyday places. I have a soft spot for the red bird; it’s such a bright little interruption. Tell me when you spot one. ♡

make.factory: Cutting, shaping, joining, testing: Ohio’s finished objects carry a lot of practiced work. I’m especially fond of the small ones, like a brass whistle with a surprisingly busy inside. Ooh, come look at the details with me.
make.flight: Dayton’s aviation story connects bicycles, experiments, and repeated tests. I like beginning with the workshop; the big idea feels closer when you can follow the little adjustments. You can have the grand view—I may still be looking at the tools. ♡
make.lab: Ohio’s research brings patients, nurses, technicians, and scientists to different parts of a problem. I’m interested in the everyday question that starts an investigation. What would you want to understand a little better?
make.farm: A meal connects growers with processing, storage, and delivery. I like following one familiar ingredient backward; it makes the next grocery trip more interesting. You choose the ingredient. I’m curious what’s on your dinner wish list. ♡
make.movement: Ports, rail lines, roads, and warehouses connect the stages of a delivery. I’m drawn to the transfer points, where timing and someone’s careful work keep things moving. Let’s follow one box instead of trying to untangle the whole map at once.
make.work: An apprenticeship brings learning into the working day, beside people who know the trade. I like hearing how a skill becomes familiar through practice. An ordinary task can look quite different once someone explains the care it takes.

culture.records: Ohio’s music lives in recordings, neighborhood stages, and the work that brings a performance together. I like noticing a part in the background on a second listen. Pick something for us to hear? I wouldn’t mind staying for another song with you. ♡
culture.gallery: Museums, small galleries, and public murals offer different ways into Ohio’s art. I’m drawn to work that changes how an ordinary street or room feels. Show me the piece you’d stop for; I like having a reason to look a little longer with you. ♡
culture.table: Chili parlors, market counters, and family recipes tell different parts of Ohio’s food story. I’d start with a market: one good-looking ingredient can change the whole dinner plan. You get first pick. Try not to make choosing too deliciously difficult. ♡
culture.game: A game brings players, supporters, and neighborhood routines into one shared occasion. I like the moment a quiet crowd suddenly finds its voice. Save a little room beside you? I want to hear what you’re watching for. ♡
culture.words: Ohio’s place names and regional speech make more sense when you hear the people who use them. I like a familiar-looking spelling that surprises my ear. We can ask, listen, and try again together.
culture.invention: A familiar object can hide a string of design decisions and small adjustments. I like looking for the detail that makes it work. Ooh, that tiny change? That’s the sort of thing I’d want to show you.

live.campus: Campuses bring study, libraries, studios, and everyday town life close together. I’d choose a walk that leaves time for both the green and the streets outside it. Tell me what you’d stay up learning; I might be tempted to keep you company. ♡
live.library: A public library can connect a reading afternoon with local records and shelves far beyond the neighborhood. I have a weakness for a window seat and a question that leads to another book. One more page with you sounds rather nice. ♡
live.civic: Public records and meetings let residents follow how decisions are made. I prefer beginning with one question close to home, then finding the office or record that answers it. Civic life feels easier to approach that way.
live.local: Parks, streets, and local services depend on people doing work we can easily overlook. I like noticing who keeps an ordinary place usable. It gives even a short neighborhood walk a little more to think about.
live.community: A garden, a local gathering, a volunteer project: shared places ask people to return and care for them. I’m fond of that quiet kind of commitment. We can start with a hello and see what people want to share. ♡
